summary: Phase 6 camera-capture pipeline backend test suite — 16/16 passed against ASP.NET Core API running with CANE_CAMERA_SIMULATOR=true on http://localhost:8001 (SQLite dev DB). Verified: (1) POST /api/weighment/gross returns captureQueued=true and asynchronously creates one PurchaseImage row per enabled camera with captureStage=GROSS, imageName pattern GROSS-CAM{NN}-{seq}.jpg, non-null SHA256 fileHash; (2) POST /api/weighment/tare produces TARE-CAM{NN}-{seq}.jpg rows coexisting with GROSS rows on the same purchase; (3) JPEG files physically persist under /tmp/canefactory_images/2026-27/Images/YYYY/MM/DD/PUR-{id}/ and start with FF D8 magic bytes; (4) GET /api/images/{id}/file returns image/jpeg raw bytes (200) and 404 for missing id; (5) POST /api/purchases/{id}/images/capture (synchronous) returns results[] with cameraConfigId/cameraNumber/success/imageId/imageName, correctly increments sequence, and returns 400 for stage='FOO'; (6) Both kill switches (System Setting ImageCaptureEnabled=false AND CameraSystemEnabled=false) produce empty results[] with disabled message; (7) Per-camera captureEnabled=false skips that camera entirely from results and no image row is created; (8) RBAC — Operator role (Image.Create only) gets 403 on GET /api/purchases/{id}/images but 200 on POST /images/capture; Developer gets 200 on both; (9) GET /api/config/cameras/1/snapshot returns JPEG bytes and returns 409 with message for a non-existent camera id; (10) Regression — login, forced password change gate, and full Gross+Tare weighment math (Net=Gross-Tare, Cutting%=Net*pct, PurchaseAmount=FinalWeight*Rate rounded 2dp) all still pass. No production issues found in Phase 6.
critical_code_review_comments: PurchaseImages endpoint (/api/purchases/{id}/images) returns the same fileHash for every image in simulator mode because the SIMULATOR provider returns identical placeholder bytes — this is expected in this environment but in production the hash should differ per frame. Consider seeding SIMULATOR to embed a timestamp/purchaseId/sequence in the JPEG payload so integration tests can differentiate frames and catch accidental hash-collision regressions (e.g. bug where every capture writes the same buffer).

POST /api/config/cameras is upsert-by-cameraNumber (no separate PUT/{id}), and it re-encrypts a password on every call — the API forces the client to re-send `password` on a mere captureEnabled toggle. A proper PATCH /api/config/cameras/{id} that accepts partial fields would prevent operators from having to re-transmit credentials over the wire whenever they flip a capture toggle in the UI.

Manual re-capture POST accepts body as Dictionary<string,string> instead of a typed DTO — a client sending {"stage":123} (non-string) will 400 with a deserialization error rather than the intended 'Stage must be GROSS or TARE' message. Introduce a small CaptureRequest DTO for clean validation UX.

Kill-switch response (empty results[]) returns HTTP 200 with a message — arguably correct (the operation was accepted and consciously no-oped), but a Flutter UI reading only `results.length==2` would silently succeed on 'captured 0/0'. Consider adding a `captureDisabled: true` boolean in the response for explicit client-side branching.

Image file endpoint GET /api/images/{id}/file streams JPEGs without a Cache-Control header — since a captured image row is immutable, `Cache-Control: private, max-age=31536000, immutable` would meaningfully reduce round-trips when the Flutter viewer scrolls through a purchase's evidence gallery.
